_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description:
A tall image on a phone viewport (390x844) still maps regions correctly: the conversation read a 400x1600 PNG with read_image. "The overlay" is ".image-comment-overlay"; "the frame" is ".image-comment-overlay .image-comment-frame" (it shrink-wraps the image, so its box is the image's displayed pixels and a fraction of it is a fraction of the image). "Drag from (a, b) to (c, d)" means: move the mouse over the frame at offsets (a × its width, b × its height) from its top-left, press the left button, move to (c × width, d × height) in N steps (5 unless said otherwise), and release; read the frame's box with getBoundingClientRect when computing the offsets. "Drag the middle half" is a drag from (0.25, 0.25) to (0.75, 0.75). The open comment dialog has its title ".diff-viewer-comment-dialog-handle" (it names the region being commented on), its input ".diff-viewer-comment-input" and its button "Add Comment" (name exactly that). window.geometry() returns the WxH+X+Y region the dialog title names; window.middleHalf(W, H) returns "ok" if that region is the middle half of a WxH image, within tolerance, and otherwise what is off; window.keepGeometry() keeps the current geometry for later, and window.kept(i) returns the i-th one kept (from 0). Check the message input's (data-testid "message-input") value with an eval comparing it to the exact string, building it with window.kept(i) where it says G or Gi; \n is a newline. Perform the steps in order.
1. Navigate to /c/image. Wait (up to 30s) for the first ".screenshot-tool .commentable-image" (the image) to be visible. Click it.
2. The hint that gates other tests is hidden at phone width, so wait on the whole-image button instead: it is disabled until the image reports its size, which is also when drawing becomes live. The overlay's button "Comment on the whole image" should be enabled.
3. The frame shrink-wraps the image, which is what makes a fraction of the frame a fraction of the image; and the whole image is reachable without scrolling, so every part of it can be dragged on: window.shrinkWraps(844) should return exactly "ok".
4. Drag the middle half. window.middleHalf(400, 1600) should return exactly "ok".

steps.expression: (() => { const frame = document.querySelector('.image-comment-overlay .image-comment-frame'); const r = frame.getBoundingClientRect(); window.__fr = r; return 'ready'; })()
